svg.text: Inside the bench — one datagram per tick
One controller drives three modules and one subprocess; only the sender touches the network.
main.py
controller and rate loop
scenario.py
kinematic model
encoder_client.py
the codec seam
cpm_encode
C++ subprocess
sender.py
Boot — configuration and the helper process, before any datagram
load the environment, then load and validate the scenario file
start the encoder
spawn the subprocess, open the pipes
Rate loop — ten times per second, until the scenario ends
sample(t)
the object's state at scenario time t
encode(content)
one JSON line on standard input
the UPER bytes, base64 on standard output
send(bytes) — one datagram, 58 bytes nominal
[TX] one log line: sequence, scenario time, byte count
An encode error costs one datagram: the client raises, the loop logs
[ENC-SKIP] and the next tick sends normally.
If the subprocess dies, the client respawns it with backoff. The bench
stays alive and keeps logging, which is what makes the failure visible.
